ai-at-work.title: Flock reportedly tries to shrink workforce with employee buyouts
ai-at-work.excerpt: Without buyouts, Flock would "almost certainly" need to lay off staff.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Flock is offering voluntary buyouts to employees rather than doing straight layoffs, which TechCrunch reports the company says it would otherwise have to do. This matters because it signals how even workplace collaboration platforms are struggling with unit economics and the post-pandemic hiring hangover that hit the entire sector. Look, offering buyouts instead of pink slips is objectively nicer, but let's be honest: when a company that's supposed to help you communicate is quietly shrinking, someone's already made the hard decision about their burn rate.

ai-at-work.title: AI governance moves from observability to provable control
ai-at-work.excerpt: As artificial intelligence agents move from experimental tools into production systems, enterprise governance is being forced to answer a harder question. It is no longer enough to know what an agent
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are shifting from just watching what their AI systems do to actually proving they're authorized to do it, with documented reasons for every action. This matters because digital workplace leaders are now accountable for AI decisions in ways they weren't before, which means audit trails and governance frameworks just became mandatory, not optional. Welcome to the compliance theater version of AI, where your AI's permission slip is just as important as what it actually accomplishes.

ai-at-work.title: What to expect during Oracle’s ‘AI Cyberattacks Are Escalating: How to Secure Your Data Now’ event: Join theCUBE on Sept. 22
ai-at-work.excerpt: At a time when AI is introducing new risks to global systems, Oracle Corp. is shifting enterprise security toward the data layer. This approach, based on a three-pronged strategy to secure at source,
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Oracle is hosting a webinar on September 22nd where they'll pitch their data-layer security approach to counter AI-driven cyberattacks, focusing on securing data at source, in motion, and through resilience. This matters because AI is genuinely making attacks faster and more sophisticated, so digital workplace leaders need to understand where their actual vulnerabilities sit. Here's the thing though: Oracle selling you a three-pronged security strategy is like a locksmith telling you that locks are the answer to crime. The real work is figuring out which prong actually applies to your mess.

ai-at-work.title: At AGNTCon Europe, ensuring AI agents don’t kill us all
ai-at-work.excerpt: At this past week’s AGNTCon + MCPCon Europe 2026 conference in Amsterdam, the buzz around agentic artificial intelligence was palpable – but nobody was particularly worried that AI was going to kill u
ai-at-work.dwp_take: A bunch of people gathered in Amsterdam last week to talk about AI agents actually doing useful work instead of destroying humanity, and somehow the frontier model vendors who would actually know what's happening couldn't be bothered to show up. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand the gap between AI hype and what's actually deployable today, and that gap apparently includes the people building the most advanced models. Look, when the people most responsible for AI safety are too busy with their own boardrooms to attend a conference about making AI work safely, you know we're in that special moment where everyone's building the plane while flying it.

tools-tech.excerpt: Browsing the web on Android sure ain’t what it used to be. Earlier this week, we talked about how the Vivaldi web browser is bringing support for Chrome extensions to Android. Vivaldi has the same Chr
tools-tech.dwp_take: Vivaldi browser just brought Chrome extension support to Android, which means mobile users can finally customize their browsing experience the way desktop users have for years. For digital workplace folks, this matters because remote workers relying on mobile devices can now use productivity extensions like password managers, ad blockers, and collaboration tools on the go. Honestly, it's wild that this took so long to happen, but better late than never when your team is juggling work across five different devices.

digital-culture.title: I use AI to save time. So why am I working more?
digital-culture.excerpt: This year, I’ve been building an AI social media production pipeline to promote the 25+ shows on the Autistic Culture Podcast Network. It took me a week of effort, but I managed to program Claude Code
digital-culture.dwp_take: Someone built an AI pipeline that cut their social media posting from a full day down to background automation, yet they're somehow working more hours overall. The digital workplace keeps falling into the same trap: efficiency gains get consumed by scope creep, not reclaimed as actual time off. Here's the real insight nobody wants to hear: AI didn't save them time, it just made them better equipped to say yes to more work.

digital-culture.title: Join the WIRED World Fair in Miami on November 4
digital-culture.excerpt: For one day only, WIRED is bringing the technologies, people, and cultural forces transforming our world off the page and into real life.
digital-culture.dwp_take: WIRED is hosting a one-day conference in Miami on November 4 to showcase emerging technologies and the people shaping them. For digital workplace pros, these events are solid networking opportunities where you can actually talk to practitioners instead of reading another LinkedIn post about the future of work. That said, if you're paying conference prices to hear someone explain AI again, you might want to check the actual schedule first because "transforming our world" sounds like every tech event since 2016.

industry-news.title: Meta’s New AI Chip Is Coming in 2027: Arke Targets Lower AI Costs
industry-news.excerpt: Meta plans to deploy its MTIA 450 Arke AI chip in 2027 as it looks to cut inference costs, energy use and reliance on general-purpose GPUs. The post Meta’s New AI Chip Is Coming in 2027: Arke Targets
industry-news.dwp_take: Meta is building its own AI chip called Arke, due in 2027, designed to reduce inference costs and energy consumption while cutting dependence on third-party GPUs. This matters because it signals the end of the GPU monopoly era, meaning organizations will soon have real alternatives that could reshape AI infrastructure budgets and availability. Here's the thing though: 2027 is forever in tech time, so don't cancel your Nvidia contracts just yet.

industry-news.title: Hackers Are Using Passkey Updates as a New Microsoft Phishing Hook
industry-news.excerpt: Microsoft warns attackers are using passkey and MFA update requests to phish employees, hijack sessions, and access Microsoft 365 data. The post Hackers Are Using Passkey Updates as a New Microsoft Ph
industry-news.dwp_take: Criminals are now baiting employees with fake passkey and MFA update notifications to steal credentials and break into Microsoft 365 accounts. This matters because your workplace security posture depends on people actually recognizing the difference between real security upgrades and social engineering attacks, and right now that's getting harder. The irony is thick: we push passkeys as the more secure option, but users still can't tell a real update from a convincing fake, which means we're just giving hackers a shinier lure to cast.

industry-news.title: UAE Cyber Chief Says Country Faced 640,000 Cyberattacks in One Day
industry-news.excerpt: The UAE faced 640,000 cyberattacks in one day, its cyber chief says, highlighting risks from unpatched software, ransomware, and deepfakes. The post UAE Cyber Chief Says Country Faced 640,000 Cyberatt
industry-news.dwp_take: The UAE's cyber chief reported their country absorbed 640,000 cyberattacks in a single day, with vulnerabilities stemming from unpatched software, ransomware campaigns, and deepfake threats. Digital workplace pros need to care because this scale of attack activity shows that security isn't some IT department problem anymore, it's a workplace infrastructure crisis that affects every employee and system.
